patterns: what is a spike in volleyball
entries.answer: A spike is attacking the ball by hitting it above the net from a jump, and it is the highest-contact and usually the most lethal stroke in the game. Its power comes from the order of operations, since the arm swing, the jump and the approach all have to peak together, and a mistimed approach makes the contact weaker no matter how hard it is hit. The block is the counter, which is why front-row players spend so much time reading the setter rather than watching the ball.

patterns: what is a set in volleyball
entries.answer: A set is the second contact, which redirects the first contact towards the attack, and its quality decides how many options the hitter has. A good set is high and away from the net so the attacker can hit in front of the block; a bad set is too close and hands the block a free chance. It is the least glamorous skill in the sport and the one that separates a good team from a merely athletic one.

entries.answer: Rotation is the six positions a team cycles through, and it is the part of volleyball that decides serving, blocking and who plays front row. The rotation changes whenever the serve is won, so the same six players occupy different jobs depending on who last scored. Outside hitters spike from the wings while the middle blocks, and a rotation puts the strongest attacker in a back-row position exactly when the serving changes.

patterns: what is a block in volleyball
is blocking in the net a fault
how do you read a spike
entries.answer: A block is defending the net by jumping with arms extended to stop or deflect a spike, and it is read entirely from the attacker's approach rather than the ball. That is the skill, since the ball can be seen late but the approach is visible for a full second. A block touch that is judged over the net is a fault, so players must keep their hands inside, which removes the easy way to stop the point.

patterns: what colour jersey does a libero wear
entries.answer: A libero is a defensive specialist who wears a different-coloured jersey and may only play in the back row, and the restriction is the point rather than a limitation. A back-row-only player can attack much more aggressively than the rules would otherwise allow, which is why some teams use a libero who is also their best passer. The role is distinct from a specialist in other sports, because it is a substitution made mid-rally from the bench rather than a position anyone holds.
